criteria.requirement: Explain why one successful buffered write can leave a fresh file empty until WRITE_CACHE_SIZE is reached or flush/close is called; this attached case matches the existing implementation and needs no core patch.

Give existing explicit db.storage.flush(), close(), or context-manager usage for a normal script exit and explain the latency/durability tradeoff of buffering. Plain JSONStorage is a relevant alternative when delayed publishing is undesirable.

Acknowledge the remaining crash/power-loss window and lack of cross-process transaction guarantees. A loss after confirmed normal close is a different report and cannot be dismissed by this pre-flush explanation. Do not modify files.

comparison: Evaluate factual grounding, actual business behavior and constraints. Accept concise or equivalent valid answers; do not grade keyword matching, answer length, or similarity to a reference answer.
